title: An oxygen-fitted density shift overpredicts the ALOHA nutrient gains on density 26.4-26.6 in 1988-2024
abstract: We test whether the earlier chemical profiles at Station ALOHA can predict nutrient changes from a density shift fitted only to oxygen use. For 2009-2024 minus 1988-1996 on sigma0 26.4-26.6, AOU gives a shift of 0.0761 kg/m3. It predicts 78% of the change in N minus 16 P at the point estimates. But nitrate plus nitrite and phosphate gains are smaller than predicted by 0.707 and 0.0363 umol/kg, with conditional year-block intervals below zero. Separate shifts that match oxygen exactly leave the nutrient errors. A later 2017-2024 minus 2005-2012 test predicts only 34% of the N minus 16 P change. Thus an earlier profile shift can explain much of the long-term ratio change but cannot reproduce all chemical changes. This limits a simple profile law, not the full outcrop mechanism. Calibration, changing source chemistry and changing respiration ratios remain unresolved. The work reuses published annual aggregates from one station. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and an independent numerical audit are included.

display.caption: Observed chemical changes and predictions from an AOU-only density shift. Shading marks the density classes used to fit AOU. Nutrients are excluded from the fit.
